content.content:
# The in-app browser by a person (LLP 1133.024 D11–D13, stage 4)

What no tool can do here: look at Safari's view and a Custom Tab over the
app, close them, and see the default browser open. `test/excord.mjs` drives
the rest under the agent: the `browser` ticket on iOS and Android, and the
link followed where the page does not show over the app (macOS, the web).
Write down the commit, the device and its OS version beside each result.

Excord carries the module: an embed's title and an attachment's row open
their page. Start its fixture server first, which serves a channel whose
messages have link embeds:
`bun apps/excord/fixture/server.ts --world transcript --reset-on-identify`.

## iPhone or the iOS simulator, iOS 17 or later

`bun host/apple/build.mjs --ios excord-apple --run` (a simulator;
`--device --run` on a phone).

1. **Over the conversation.** Open #general and scroll to a message with a
   link preview ("exact: keep the visible row anchored"). Tap its title:
   Safari's view slides up over the conversation with Safari's own bar and
   a Done button, at github.com.
2. **Done returns.** Tap Done: the view goes and the conversation is where
   it was, at the same message.
3. **One at a time.** With the page shown, nothing else in Excord can be
   tapped; the next tap after Done opens again.
4. **The app reads nothing.** Sign in to a site in the page, close it, open
   Safari: Excord never sees the page's cookies (nothing to see; this is
   the platform's).

## Mac

`bun host/apple/build.mjs excord-apple --run`.

5. **The default browser.** Click the same title: the page opens in the
   Mac's default browser, beside Excord, and Excord stays as it was. No
   sheet or web view appears in Excord.

## Android phone with Chrome, Android 12 or later

../../docs/reference.md:1934:the platform would call (`delivery: "substituted"`).

```text
resource status = status(car) with minute as shape Status
```

The source receives `car`, then `minute`; changes to either ask again. `with`
accepts one or more expressions before `as shape`, and the call may be empty.
Call arguments identify the answer and should include its account or tenant.
Inputs after `with` are request context: they reach the source and trigger a new
request, but do not change persisted-answer identity. On hosts that persist
eligible store-reading answers, a returning launch can show the kept answer for
the same call arguments while the source is unready, even when a `with` input
changed. During a live replacement request, the prior displayed value may remain
visible even when call arguments changed, so private-data views must gate it by
owner and authorization. Neither call arguments nor `with` make a resource wait
for an upstream request to succeed. The default web JS target keeps no persisted
resource answers; see
[the platform scope](../llp/1027.005-resource-identity-and-request-context.rfc.md#d5--where-it-applies-and-the-gap-it-leaves).
The minute must already contain the current sample for the first ask; a timer
can update it thereafter. Use `refresh` or `refreshes` for values whose only job
is forcing another ask. Await true asynchronous prerequisites, such as a valid
session, inside the data source before issuing the dependent request.
anything else changes the router, which the router refuses (`lower-replace-root`), a count before a plural noun, `${n} cards`
(`lower-count-plural`), a row of the app's records that searches another table of them,
`users.filter(u => u.id == p.userId)` in `for p in posts` (`lower-row-lookup`), a
row that walks its own list, `tokens.slice(0, i)` in `for t, i in tokens`
(`lower-row-own-list`), a
symbol by an alias, not its role (`lower-symbol-alias`), a

launch's `time.epochAtZero` or `time.seed` as a resource's identifying argument, or a

#!/bin/bash
# The benchmarked build: Everbloom for arm64 iOS devices, release (production) mode.
#
#   DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=ABCDE12345 scripts/build-ios-device.sh   signed for that team (automatic signing)
#   scripts/build-ios-device.sh                               no team: code signing disabled (ad-hoc)
#
# Result: build/ios-device/Everbloom.app
#
# Exact assembles and signs its .app itself (no Xcode project).
#
# With DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: Xcode first builds a never-shipped stub app with the same
# bundle id under that team with -allowProvisioningUpdates and
# -allowProvisioningDeviceRegistration, so Xcode's automatic signing creates (or
# refreshes) the team's development profile for the id, registering a connected
# iPhone. Exact's device release build (`ios --device --release --no-install`)
# then signs with that profile and the team's Apple Development identity. Exact
# builds a development-signed device app for a phone this Mac knows, so the
# benchmark iPhone must have been connected to this Mac (xcrun devicectl list
# devices shows it); EXACT_PHONE=<udid|name> picks one of several.
#
# Without DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: Exact's only phone-less device packaging is its
# distribution archive (`--archive --unsigned`, ad-hoc signed, no profile, no
# team), which refuses a bundle without an app icon. For that build only, a
# plain white placeholder icon (scripts/unsigned-placeholder-icon.png) is named
# in app.json and removed again afterwards; the signed build has no icon.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
APP_DIR="$ROOT/everbloom"
OUT="$ROOT/build/ios-device"
BUNDLE_ID="dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.exact"
BUN="${BUN:-$HOME/.bun-1.4.2/bin/bun}"
export PATH="$(dirname "$BUN"):$PATH"

mkdir -p "$OUT"
rm -rf "$OUT/Everbloom.app" "$OUT/Everbloom.ipa" "$OUT/Payload"

if [[ -n "${DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-}" ]]; then
  STUB_DD="$OUT/stub-derived"
  xcodebuild -project "$ROOT/scripts/signing-stub/Stub.xcodeproj" -scheme Stub -configuration Release \
    -destination generic/platform=iOS -derivedDataPath "$STUB_DD" \
    -allowProvisioningUpdates -allowProvisioningDeviceRegistration \
    DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" STUB_BUNDLE_ID="$BUNDLE_ID" build >"$OUT/stub-build.log" 2>&1 \
    || { echo "Xcode could not sign the stub for team $DEVELOPMENT_TEAM; see $OUT/stub-build.log" >&2; exit 1; }
  STUB_APP="$STUB_DD/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Stub.app"
  [[ -f "$STUB_APP/embedded.mobileprovision" ]] || { echo "no provisioning profile in the stub build" >&2; exit 1; }
  cp "$STUB_APP/embedded.mobileprovision" "$OUT/team.mobileprovision"
  # The identity Xcode signed the stub with, as the SHA-1 Exact's EXACT_IDENTITY takes.
  IDENTITY="$(codesign -dvvv "$STUB_APP" 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^Authority=\(Apple Development: .*\)$/\1/p' | head -1)"
  SHA1="$(security find-identity -v -p codesigning | grep -F "\"$IDENTITY\"" | head -1 | awk '{print $2}')"
  [[ -n "$SHA1" ]] || { echo "no keychain identity matches \"$IDENTITY\"" >&2; exit 1; }
  (cd "$APP_DIR" && EXACT_IDENTITY="$SHA1" EXACT_PROFILE="$OUT/team.mobileprovision" \
    "$BUN" exact.mjs ios --device --release --no-install)
  BUILT="$(ls -td "$APP_DIR"/target/clients/*/"$BUNDLE_ID"/ios/aarch64-apple-ios/*/production/standalone/Everbloom.app | head -1)"
  ditto "$BUILT" "$OUT/Everbloom.app"
else
  MANIFEST="$APP_DIR/app.json"
  cp "$MANIFEST" "$OUT/app.json.orig"
  cp "$ROOT/scripts/unsigned-placeholder-icon.png" "$APP_DIR/.exact/unsigned-placeholder-icon.png"
  restore() { cp "$OUT/app.json.orig" "$MANIFEST"; rm -f "$OUT/app.json.orig" "$APP_DIR/.exact/unsigned-placeholder-icon.png"; }
  trap restore EXIT
  "$BUN" -e 'const f=process.argv[1]; const m=JSON.parse(await Bun.file(f).text());
    m.icons=[{src: ".exact/unsigned-placeholder-icon.png", sizes: "1024x1024", type: "image/png"}];
    await Bun.write(f, JSON.stringify(m, null, 2) + "\n");' "$MANIFEST"
  (cd "$APP_DIR" && "$BUN" exact.mjs ios --device --release --archive "$OUT/Everbloom.ipa" --unsigned)
  (cd "$OUT" && ditto -x -k Everbloom.ipa . && mv Payload/*.app "$OUT/Everbloom.app" && rm -rf Payload)
fi

echo "$OUT/Everbloom.app"

#!/bin/bash
# The benchmarked build: Everbloom for arm64 iOS devices, release (production) mode.
#
#   DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=ABCDE12345 scripts/build-ios-device.sh   signed for that team (automatic signing)
#   scripts/build-ios-device.sh                               no team: code signing disabled (ad-hoc, for re-signing)
#
# Result: build/ios-device/Everbloom.app (and build/ios-device/Everbloom.ipa).
#
# Exact assembles and signs its .app itself (no Xcode project). For automatic
# signing, Xcode first builds a stub app with the same bundle id under
# DEVELOPMENT_TEAM with -allowProvisioningUpdates, which makes Xcode create (or
# refresh) the team's development profile for the id and every registered
# device; Exact's build then signs with that profile and the team's Apple
# Development identity.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
APP_DIR="$ROOT/everbloom"
OUT="$ROOT/build/ios-device"
BUNDLE_ID="dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.exact"
BUN="${BUN:-$HOME/.bun-1.4.2/bin/bun}"
export PATH="$(dirname "$BUN"):$PATH"

mkdir -p "$OUT"
rm -rf "$OUT/Everbloom.app" "$OUT/Everbloom.ipa" "$OUT/Payload"

if [[ -n "${DEVELOPMENT_TEAM:-}" ]]; then
  STUB_DD="$OUT/stub-derived"
  xcodebuild -project "$ROOT/scripts/signing-stub/Stub.xcodeproj" -scheme Stub -configuration Release \
    -destination generic/platform=iOS -derivedDataPath "$STUB_DD" -allowProvisioningUpdates \
    DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" STUB_BUNDLE_ID="$BUNDLE_ID" build >"$OUT/stub-build.log" 2>&1 \
    || { echo "Xcode could not sign the stub for team $DEVELOPMENT_TEAM; see $OUT/stub-build.log" >&2; exit 1; }
  PROFILE="$STUB_DD/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Stub.app/embedded.mobileprovision"
  [[ -f "$PROFILE" ]] || { echo "no provisioning profile in the stub build ($PROFILE)" >&2; exit 1; }
  cp "$PROFILE" "$OUT/team.mobileprovision"
  # The identity Xcode signed the stub with: its SHA-1, as Exact's EXACT_IDENTITY takes it.
  IDENTITY="$(codesign -dvvv "$STUB_DD/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Stub.app" 2>&1 | sed -n 's/^Authority=\(Apple Development: .*\)$/\1/p' | head -1)"
  SHA1="$(security find-identity -v -p codesigning | grep -F "\"$IDENTITY\"" | head -1 | awk '{print $2}')"
  [[ -n "$SHA1" ]] || { echo "no keychain identity matches \"$IDENTITY\"" >&2; exit 1; }
  (cd "$APP_DIR" && EXACT_IDENTITY="$SHA1" EXACT_PROFILE="$OUT/team.mobileprovision" \
    "$BUN" exact.mjs ios --device --release --archive "$OUT/Everbloom.ipa")
else
  # CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO: no team, so the bundle is ad-hoc signed with no profile.
  (cd "$APP_DIR" && "$BUN" exact.mjs ios --device --release --archive "$OUT/Everbloom.ipa" --unsigned)
fi

(cd "$OUT" && ditto -x -k Everbloom.ipa . && mv Payload/*.app "$OUT/Everbloom.app" && rm -rf Payload)
echo "$OUT/Everbloom.app"

# Building Everbloom (Exact)

All commands run from the project root on macOS (Apple silicon). The app is in `everbloom/`;
Exact itself is cloned into `vendor/exact2/` by step 1 (Exact has no releases: an app builds
against a checkout, by path).

> **iOS needs Xcode 27.** The pinned Exact commit (and every public Exact commit) compiles its
> UIKit host against the iOS 27 SDK (`UIArrangementViewController`, iOS 27 `AVAudioSession`
> notifications and other iOS 27 APIs). With Xcode 26.x the Swift compile of `ExactKit` fails.
> If Xcode 27 is not `xcode-select`'s, point the commands at it:
> `export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-27.app/Contents/Developer`.
> See `NOTES.md`: on the machine this was written on only Xcode 26.6 was installed, so the
> iOS builds below were not run to completion there.

## 1. Install dependencies

Prerequisites: Xcode 27 (with an iOS 27 Simulator runtime), `rustup`, `git`, `curl`, and for
Android the Android SDK (`ANDROID_HOME`, default `~/Library/Android/sdk`) with an NDK and a JDK 17+
(Android Studio's bundled JBR is picked up automatically).

```sh
scripts/install.sh
```

It clones Exact (`expo/exact` at `fc14919528fb76ca8de3e8c8d9ef91853f923a17`) and Ibex
(`expo/ibex` at `a0183568e8229b8243629cdb26cd4a88ac4e2abd`) into `vendor/`, installs Bun 1.4.2
into `~/.bun-1.4.2` (beside any other Bun), runs Exact's `setup` (pinned Rust 1.97.0, Hermes
bundles for macOS and iOS, offline crates), adds the Rust targets `aarch64-apple-ios`,
`aarch64-apple-ios-sim` and `aarch64-linux-android`, installs the app's package
(`@exact/in-app-browser`, from the Exact checkout), and builds the Android Hermes bundle from
the Ibex checkout (about 10 minutes, once; cached in `~/.cache/exact/hermes-android`). For Android
it also needs the SDK platform 37.2:

```sh
"$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager" "platforms;android-37.2"
```

## 2. iOS device release build (benchmarked)

Signed for a team (automatic signing; the Mac's Xcode must be signed in to an account of that team):

```sh
DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=ABCDE12345 scripts/build-ios-device.sh
```

Without a team (code signing disabled: the bundle is ad-hoc signed, no profile):

```sh
scripts/build-ios-device.sh
```

Result: **`build/ios-device/Everbloom.app`** (and `build/ios-device/Everbloom.ipa`).

Exact builds the `.app` itself (Cargo, SwiftPM, its own bundler and `codesign`), not through an
Xcode project. With `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` set, the script first builds a never-shipped stub Xcode
project (`scripts/signing-stub/`) with the same bundle id and `-allowProvisioningUpdates`, so Xcode's
automatic signing creates the team's development profile, then runs Exact's device release build
signed with that profile and the team's Apple Development identity
(`bun exact.mjs ios --device --release --archive …` with `EXACT_PROFILE`/`EXACT_IDENTITY`).
Without it, it runs the same build with `--unsigned`. The first build takes 10–15 minutes.

dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.exact
```

Omit `--environment-variables` to use `https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api`. The app reads
`SHOP_API_URL` from its launch environment (through its Swift module, `everbloom/modules/apple/Shop.swift`).

## 4. iOS Simulator build

Boot an iPhone simulator first (`xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 17 Pro"`; or set `EXACT_SIM` to a
name or UDID). Then:

```sh
scripts/build-ios-simulator.sh
```

Result: **`build/ios-simulator/Everbloom.app`** (the script also installs it on the booted simulator).
Install and launch with the endpoint override:

```sh
xcrun simctl install booted build/ios-simulator/Everbloom.app
SIMCTL_CHILD_SHOP_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/api xcrun simctl launch booted dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.exact
```

The marker line: `xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "SHOPBENCH"'`.

`scripts/dev-proxy.ts` (`~/.bun-1.4.2/bin/bun scripts/dev-proxy.ts 8787`) is a stand-in for the replay
server that forwards to mock.shop; stop it to see the error state, start it again and tap Retry.

## 5. Android release APK

```sh
scripts/build-android.sh                                            # default endpoint
SHOP_API_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8787/api scripts/build-android.sh  # endpoint fixed at build time
```

Result: **`build/android/Everbloom-release.apk`** (`everbloom/target/android/app/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk`).

```sh
adb install -r build/android/Everbloom-release.apk
adb shell am start -n dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.exact/dev.exact.app.MainActivity
```

The endpoint is read at build time (`app.json` `env`: `SHOP_API_URL` from the environment, else
`everbloom/.env.local`, else `everbloom/.env`) and inlined into the data module. Plain HTTP is
allowed: Exact's `fetch` on Android uses its own Rust sockets, which Android's cleartext policy does
not govern, and the app's grants admit `http:` and `https:` to any host.

## 6. Build modes and toolchains

| Build | Mode |
|---|---|
| iOS device | Exact production: `ios --device --release --archive` (Rust `release` profile, Swift whole-module `-O`, `EXACT_UPDATE_TRUST=production`, plan and Hermes bytecode baked in, no development server, no agent, no hot reload, no dev menu; update store `"0"`, so no update checks) |
| iOS Simulator | The same production mode for the simulator: `ios --release` (Exact's "build that ships", the most production-like it offers on the simulator) |
| Android | Rust `release` profile (fat LTO) + Gradle `assembleRelease`, signed with the debug key |

| Tool | Version |
|---|---|
| Exact | `expo/exact` `fc14919528fb76ca8de3e8c8d9ef91853f923a17` (2026-11-10) |
| Bun | 1.4.2 (pinned by Exact) |
| Rust | 1.97.0 (pinned by Exact's `rust-toolchain.toml`) |
| Hermes | 260318099.0.4 (Ibex bundle `hermes-vanilla-d412d3bd8512-v5`; Android built from Ibex `a0183568`) |
| Xcode | 27 required (iOS 27 SDK); this machine had 26.6 (17F113), which fails |
| Android | SDK platform 37.2, NDK 29.0.14206865, Gradle 9.8.0 (wrapper), JDK 21 (Android Studio JBR), CMake 3.22.1 (SDK) for Hermes |
| macOS | 26 (Darwin 25.5) |

50:  (it stays reachable when the page scrolls) instead of scrolling away with the carousel.
51:  The Add to cart bar sits below the scroll area rather than over it. Option pills wrap onto
52:  more lines when they do not fit. Picking a pill selects the variant matching all current
53:  options with the new value; if no variant has that combination, the first variant with the
54:  picked value.
55:- **Collection screen.** The navigation bar, description and sort chips stay fixed; the product
56:  grid below them is the scrolling container (`product-grid`), a virtualized list of rows of
57:  two cards. The sort chips scroll horizontally when they do not fit. The title shows the
58:  collection's title from Home while the collection loads.
59:- **Home.** The "See all" link in the design is not in the spec and is omitted. The header
60:  scrolls with the content ("the whole screen scrolls").
61:- **Errors.** A failed first page shows the full error state; a failed later page (collection,
62:  search) shows an inline "Couldn’t load products" with Retry at the end of the list, keeping
63:  the loaded rows.
64:- **Search.** Shows a spinner while the first page of a query loads. "1 result" is singular.
65:- **Empty cart.** "Start shopping" switches to the Home tab.
66:- **Status bar / dark mode.** Colors are the design's fixed light palette on every system theme.

content.text:
With Xcode 27.2 the iOS app builds and every Done item checks out on the iOS 27.2 Simulator, except the signed device build, which I didn't run. I checked the identifiers and the walkthrough with an XCUITest that drives the installed release build by bundle ID.

**Done items on the release simulator build:**
- **Identifiers:** XCUITest found every identifier in the spec's table.
- **Walkthrough:** passes in full.
  - Home loads, and each of the four sorts reloads the collection.
  - The collection grid scrolls to the end of its products (4 pages).
  - The product carousel swipes, the option pills switch the variant, a recommendation opens another product, and Back returns.
  - Add to cart switches to Cart with the badge showing 1, and the stepper changes the subtotal from $75.00 to $150.00.
  - Check out opens the checkout page in Safari's in-app view.
  - Reducing the quantity to 0 removes the line and badge and shows the empty cart.
  - Search returns results and scrolls.
- **Error state:** launched with `SHOP_API_URL` pointing at a stopped local proxy, Home shows the error state. After I started the proxy, Retry loaded Home, and the proxy logged the request. That also confirms the launch-time endpoint override works.
- **Log marker:** `SHOPBENCH home_ready` appears exactly once per launch (checked over two launches). The only other log lines from the app come from Apple's frameworks.
- **First frame:** the app's first frame is the Home skeleton.
- **Android:** after these changes the release APK still launches on the emulator and Home loads.

**Bugs found on iOS and fixed:**
- **Home was persisted between launches.** Exact saves the last answer of any data request that touches the native (Swift) module and shows it at the next launch. The endpoint lookup touched it, so Home came back from the previous session. That broke the no-persistence rule, the skeleton first frame, and the error state. The endpoint is now looked up once at launch in a separate step, and the data requests no longer touch the native module.
- **The Cart summary sat under the tab bar on iOS**, because iOS lays each screen out full-height. The tab bar now sits over the screens, as in the design, and each tab screen leaves room for it.
- **The cart badge** now has an accessibility label with the count, so XCUITest reads "1".

**What's not verified, and one deviation:**
- **Signed device build:** not run. No iPhone has been paired with this Mac, and running it would register the bundle ID and a provisioning profile in your Apple Developer account, which I didn't want to do without asking. The no-team device build does compile and package an arm64 release app (ad-hoc signed).
- **Placeholder icon (deviation from "no custom app icon"):** for the no-team device build only, the script temporarily adds a plain white app icon and then restores `app.json`. That build has to use Exact's App Store-style packaging, which refuses to run without an icon. The signed, benchmarked build has no icon.
- **Phone must be paired for the signed build:** Exact's signed device build needs the iPhone to have been connected to the Mac at least once. This is noted in `BUILD.md`.
- **Cart error alert:** not seen, because nothing in the UI makes mock.shop return a cart error.
- **Variant prices:** no mock.shop product has variants with different prices, so I could only confirm the price shown is the selected variant's.

I also created a simulator named "Everbloom iPhone 17 Pro (27.2)" for these checks; you can delete it. `BUILD.md` and `NOTES.md` are updated with the toolchain versions and these results.

Files are in `/Users/itome/shopbench-runs/exact`:
- `BUILD.md`
- `NOTES.md`
- `build/ios-simulator/Everbloom.app`
- `build/ios-device/Everbloom.app`
- `build/android/Everbloom-release.apk`
